title: The Lighthouse
text: Every evening the lighthouse keeper climbed the spiral stairs with a lantern in one hand and a thermos in the other. The wind rattled the windows, but the great lamp turned without complaint. Ships far out at sea watched for that steady beam, and the keeper watched the ships. He knew most of them by their lights and their habits. On clear nights the horizon seemed close enough to touch; on stormy nights it vanished entirely, leaving only the sound of waves against the rocks below.

title: A Small Bakery
text: The bakery opened before sunrise, when the streets were still blue and quiet. Inside, trays of dough waited beneath clean cloths while the ovens warmed the room. By seven, the smell of bread had reached the corner and people began to drift in with sleepy faces and exact orders. The baker remembered who liked the crust dark, who wanted the loaf sliced, and who always asked whether anything sweet had just come out. It was not a complicated business, but it was a careful one.

title: Night Train
text: The night train moved through the countryside with a rhythm that made sleep almost possible. Passengers folded jackets into pillows and watched the scattered lights of farms slide past. Somewhere near the middle of the carriage, a card game ended in laughter. In the dining car, the last cups of tea grew cold while two strangers discovered they had grown up on the same road. By morning the landscape would be different, but for now the journey itself was the destination.

title: The Workshop
text: The workshop smelled of sawdust, oil, and the faint sweetness of wood shavings. Tools hung on the wall in a neat row, each one worn smooth by years of use. The old carpenter measured twice, marked the board with a pencil, and cut once. He worked slowly because slow work was often the fastest way to get it right. Outside, the afternoon light moved across the floor, and the radio played a song he had heard a thousand times without ever learning its name.

title: The Garden
text: The garden changed every week, though nobody planted anything new. First came the small green shoots, then the crowded leaves, then the bright flowers that seemed to appear overnight. Bees moved between them with serious purpose while a cat slept in the warm patch beside the wall. By late summer the tomatoes had climbed beyond their supports, and the path was narrow enough that visitors had to turn sideways. Nobody minded. The garden had simply decided to take up more space.

title: The Bookshop
text: The bookshop was narrow, tall, and impossible to browse quickly. Shelves reached the ceiling, and the ladder that rolled along them made a soft creak whenever someone searched for a title. The owner claimed to know where every book belonged, though she was often surprised by what she found. Customers came for one thing and left with three. On rainy days the windows fogged over and the shop became a small, warm world where the only urgency was deciding which story to carry home.
